newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: The Dutch sharemarket set another closing record after positive U.S. economic data boosted shares on Wall Street and pushed the Dutch bond market higher.
Dealers said trading volumes increased after the weaker than expected retail sales data for April and May.
"The performance was very strong," said one dealer.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares ended at 839.36 points, up 12.21 on the day, compared with the previous closing record of 830.77 set on Tuesday.
The market also reached a new intra-day peak, touching 839.77 points shortly before the close.
The major Dutch news announcement of the day was the first quarter profit from retailer Ahold, which showed a 69 percent increase on a year earlier.
"The result was in line with expectations," said a dealer.
The supermarkets operator also repeated its forecast that 1997 earnings would be considerably higher than those of 1996.
The shares, hit by profit taking ahead of the results, moved into positive territory after the news.
Shortly before the Ahold results, Dutch shares and bonds were boosted by news that U.S. retail sales fell in May, the third successive monthly fall.
"The U.S. data had a positive impact because it moderates inflationary fears," said the dealer.
Royal Dutch Petroleum shares were stronger from the start, gaining through the day in a move which dealers attributed to a meeting between the company and analysts in The Hague.

Retailer Vendex International, which floated a minority stake in its temporary employment and services unit Vedior VDOR.As earlier this month, finally rebounded from a sharp sell-off, putting on 4.70 guilders to finish at 108.00
Brewer Heineken was also stronger, ending 7.60 better at 338.60.
